Jematell Homes manages every phase of the process with precision and transparency, coordinating directly with the town’s permitting requirements and working within established planning and zoning guidelines.
Our team ensures your home is built efficiently, meets all municipal standards, and performs beautifully in Arizona’s climate from foundation to final walkthrough.
Building On Your Lot In Carefree

Already own land in Carefree? We build a new home on a lot you already own, or on one our licensed real estate agents help you find. Before design starts we check the lot for water, septic, access, slope and boulders, then plan the home around the land and the views. Our complete guide to building a custom home in Carefree covers each step.
Lot Rules And Height In Carefree

Carefree keeps homes low and set well back. Every residential zone caps height at 24 feet, measured from the natural grade under each point of the house, so a sloped lot does not buy extra height. Rural-70 lots need a 60 foot front and rear yard and 30 foot sides at 13 percent lot coverage, and Rural-43 lots need a 40 foot front and rear yard at 17 percent. The Town also caps how much of the lot may be disturbed at all, driveway and septic included. Our guide to Carefree zoning and setbacks lists every district.
Building Codes And Inspections In Carefree

Carefree builds to the 2018 International Residential and Building codes and the 2017 electrical code, a cycle behind Cave Creek and Fountain Hills, so a plan drawn for the town next door may need changes. Our guide to the Carefree adopted building codes lists each one. Plans go in through the Town's online permit portal, and our guide to Carefree residential permit requirements covers what goes in the package. The Town then inspects in stages from foundation to final, as our guide to Carefree building inspections explains.
Design Review And Desert Rules In Carefree

Outdoor lighting is shielded and aimed down, protected desert plants such as saguaros are inventoried and kept or relocated, and grading is limited so washes and boulders stay where they can. We design to these rules from the first sketch rather than fixing the plan later, and our answer on the desert and dark-sky design rules explains each one. Some communities add their own review on top of the Town's. Carefree Ranch caps a home at 24 feet above natural grade and sets deep setbacks, and our guide to the Carefree Ranch design guidelines walks through them.
Water And Septic In Carefree

Much of Carefree has no sewer line, so most homes use a septic system on the lot, and the water source depends on the parcel. We confirm the water source and test the soil before the home is drawn, because the septic field takes space inside the same disturbed-area limit as the house. Our guide to Maricopa County septic and well requirements explains the county's side.
Guest Houses In Carefree

Carefree allows a guest house or casita for your own household and guests, but it may not be rented apart from the main home, and no part of it may rise more than 16 feet. The state ADU law does not reach towns under 75,000 people, so the Town's own rule decides. Our Carefree guest house rules answer explains the details, and we build casitas and guest houses with a new home or on a lot you already own.
Building Costs In Carefree

How much does it cost to build a house in Carefree? On a desert lot, the water source, the septic system, the slope and rock, and any community design review move the number more than the floor plan does. Our Carefree building cost guide walks through each one. On a cost-plus build we share every subcontractor bid with you before work begins.
Activities In Carefree

Carefree offers a peaceful desert lifestyle with access to art galleries, dining, golf, and outdoor recreation. Residents enjoy seasonal events and community gatherings at the Carefree Town Center while exploring attractions and experiences throughout the area.
With hiking trails, scenic desert landscapes, and proximity to Cave Creek and North Scottsdale, Carefree delivers both tranquility and accessibility..
Education In Carefree

Carefree families are served by the Cave Creek Unified School District, along with private and charter school options throughout the North Valley. Nearby colleges and universities in Scottsdale and Phoenix provide additional opportunities for higher education.
The area’s low-density setting combined with access to quality educational resources makes Carefree a strong choice for families planning their future.

Water For A Rio Verde Foothills Home

Rio Verde Foothills has no city water line, so every home runs on a private well or on hauled water stored in a tank on the lot. Most home wells are exempt wells, with a pump rated 35 gallons per minute or less. Hauled water now comes from the EPCOR fill station that opened January 1, 2026, and the home draws from its tank through a pressure pump. Our guide on how to get water to a home in Rio Verde Foothills compares the options.

The water source also shapes the loan, because a standard FHA loan will not accept a hauled-water tank on new construction. We plan the water and the financing together. Our answer on building in Rio Verde Foothills without city water explains why.
Septic And Soil In Rio Verde

There is no sewer in the Foothills, so each home treats its wastewater in a septic system on the lot. A site and soils test sets the size of the system before the county permits it, and in the Rio Verde Foothills planning area the county rules out seepage pits in favor of shallow trench systems. Our guide to Maricopa County septic and well requirements covers the steps, and our checklist for building on rural land in Rio Verde lists everything a raw lot needs.
County Lot Rules In Rio Verde

Rio Verde and the Rio Verde Foothills are unincorporated Maricopa County, so the county reviews the plans and inspects the build. The Rural-43 zone common here needs a 40 foot front and rear yard and 20 foot side yards, with a 35 foot height limit and 25 percent lot coverage. Our guide to Maricopa County zoning and setbacks lists the other districts.

Desert washes cross many Foothills parcels, and the county's drainage clearance often decides where the house can sit. We plan the pad and driveway around it. Our guide to the Maricopa County grading and drainage permit explains the review.
Casitas And Guest Houses In Rio Verde

Since January 2026, state law requires Maricopa County to allow one attached and one detached ADU on a single-family lot, and one more detached unit on a lot of an acre or more. That extra unit needs a recorded affordable-housing deed restriction on one unit first. Our guide to the county ADU law explains the rules, and we build casitas and guest houses with a new home or on a lot you already own, with the septic and water sized for both.
Building Costs In Rio Verde

How much does it cost to build a house in Rio Verde? On raw Foothills land, the water source, the septic system, power and the driveway can move the number as much as the floor plan does. Our Rio Verde building cost guide walks through each one. On a cost-plus build we share every subcontractor bid with you before work begins.

Rio Verde offers a relaxed lifestyle centered around golf, outdoor recreation, and community connection. Residents enjoy scenic desert landscapes, walking trails, and nearby access to Scottsdale’s dining and entertainment options.
The area’s peaceful environment and strong sense of community make it an ideal place to build a custom home designed for everyday comfort.

The area’s quiet residential setting combined with access to regional educational resources makes Rio Verde appealing for families and long-term homeowners alike.

Desert Lot Rules In Scottsdale

Lots in north and east Scottsdale fall under the city's Environmentally Sensitive Lands Ordinance, which keeps part of every lot as permanent natural desert. The share runs from about 15 percent on flat lower desert to as much as 80 percent on steep hillside, so we map the buildable area before the first sketch.

Your zoning district then sets how far the home sits from each property line. A one-acre R1-43 lot needs a 40 foot front yard, 20 foot side yards and a 35 foot rear yard, under the 30 foot height limit every single-family district shares. Casitas And Guest Houses In Scottsdale

The first unit is capped at 1,000 square feet or 75 percent of the main home, whichever is less, and a detached casita can sit as close as five feet to a side or rear lot line. BUILD A HOME IN PARADISE VALLEY

Paradise Valley is a small estate town set between Camelback Mountain and Mummy Mountain, made up almost entirely of single-family homes on lots of an acre or more. Building here means designing to some of the strictest residential rules in metro Phoenix, and it rewards a builder who plans the house around the lot from the first sketch. Building In Paradise Valley

Every zoning district in Paradise Valley is built around large lots and deep yards. The base R-43 district needs a full acre per home, with 40 foot front and rear yards and 20 foot side yards, or 40 feet for a second story or a house over 24 feet tall. Total floor area is capped at 25% of the lot in every estate district, and a lot under three acres is held to 24 feet of height.

Those numbers decide how large a home can be before any design work starts, so we check the lot first: its district, its slope, its washes and whether town water and sewer reach it. Then the floor plan is drawn to fit what the lot allows, not cut back in plan review.
Construction In Paradise Valley

The Town of Paradise Valley is the permitting authority, and it enforces the 2015 International Residential Code with the 2014 National Electrical Code and the 2021 International Fire Code. That is an older cycle than Scottsdale or Phoenix, so plans drawn for a neighboring city are reworked before they are submitted. The building permit is priced from the home's construction valuation, with an in-house plan review fee on top.

The Town runs no water or sewer system and charges no municipal impact fee, so many lots need a private well or water provider and an on-site septic system, permitted through Maricopa County and the state. A new home also needs a grading and drainage plan from an Arizona registered civil engineer. We handle the permits and schedule every inspection, and you get a written update every week of construction.
Hillside Lots In Paradise Valley

When a building site has a slope of 10% or more, the Town's Hillside Development Regulations in Article XXII limit how much of the land can be disturbed: up to 60% of the site at a 10% slope, about 34% at 15% and about 13% at 25%. A Hillside Building Committee reviews the plans before the permit, so on a sloped lot the design starts with the slope analysis.
Living In Paradise Valley

Paradise Valley is known for its resort properties, quiet estate streets and views of Camelback Mountain and Mummy Mountain, with the restaurants, shopping and golf of Scottsdale and central Phoenix a short drive away. The low-density zoning that shapes every build here is also what keeps the town feeling open.
